commands.summary: Show every install on this machine against the registry: updates, pins, and evolution on your own artifacts.
commands.desc: Reads ~/.ahood/installed.json (every install `ahood <kind> add` has made on this machine, in any project; AHOOD_INSTALLED_FILE overrides the path) and asks the registry (POST /api/v1/me/status) for each artifact's latest version. Prints installed vs latest, whether an update is available, pins, and -- on artifacts you own -- whether self-evolution is on and how many proposals wait for your review. Installs recorded only in the current project's .claude/skills.lock.json (from before this file existed) are imported on first run. Needs a login (the token's 'read' scope).
flags: --json    Emit {items, plan} instead of a table.

commands.summary: Update installs that are behind, showing each one's diff and asking y/N first.
commands.desc: For every install `ahood status` reports behind (and not pinned at its version), downloads the new version, shows a unified diff against the installed files, and asks y/N per artifact before writing it -- never without consent. A pinned install is moved only to its pinned version. The write is the ordinary atomic install (`ahood <kind> add`) run in that install's own project, so its project lockfile moves with it. With no terminal to ask on, it refuses unless --yes is given. MCP servers are skipped (they can prompt for secrets): update those with `ahood mcp update`.
flags: --yes, -y   Accept every update without asking.
--dry-run   Show the diffs, change nothing.
--json      Emit {results} (requires --yes or --dry-run: there is nobody to ask).

commands.summary: Hold an install at one version so `ahood sync` never moves it past that.
commands.desc: Pins every install of <owner>/<slug> on this machine at <version> (default: the version installed now), in ~/.ahood/installed.json. `ahood sync` skips a pinned install, or offers to move it to the pinned version if it is on another one.
flags: --json    Emit {owner, slug, installs} instead of prose.

commands.summary: Remove a pin so `ahood sync` offers the latest version again.
commands.desc: Removes the pin `ahood pin` set on every install of <owner>/<slug> on this machine.
flags: --json    Emit {owner, slug, unpinned} instead of prose.

commands.summary: List the self-evolution proposals waiting for your review with their diffs, and approve or reject them.
commands.desc: Bare `ahood review` lists your pending enhancement proposals across all your artifacts (GET /api/v1/me/proposals) with their evidence: checks, sandbox and probe results, risk findings, the review window and why automatic mode held it. In a terminal it then shows each proposal's unified diff (GET /api/v1/enhancements/candidates/<id>/diff, the diff the web owner panel shows) and asks approve/reject/skip/quit; piped, it only lists. `ahood review show <id>` prints one proposal with its diff. `ahood review approve <id>` publishes the proposal as a new version (--version when it needs one chosen) and `ahood review reject <id>` discards it -- the same decision as the web owner panel. Listing needs the token's 'read' scope; the diff and deciding need its 'publish' scope.
flags: --version <semver>  (approve) The version to publish; default is the suggested next patch.
--limit <n>         (list) One page of at most n (1-100) instead of the whole queue.
--json              Emit the API response; each proposal carries its `diff` ({files, unchanged_binaries, truncated}, null with `diff_error` when unreadable).

commands.summary: Find skills, agents, MCP servers, docs, project guides, loops and prompts in the registry.
commands.desc: Searches the registry across every kind (GET /api/v1/skills, the same request as `ahood skill search`) and prints one line per result: owner/slug, kind, its one-line purpose, stars and downloads. --kind narrows to one kind (skill, agent, mcp, doc, project, loop, prompt); --sort picks the order (default: rank, the registry's recommended order; downloads for the most installed). The query may be left out when --kind or --sort is given, which browses instead of searching. Needs a login.
flags: --kind <kind>   Only this kind: skill, agent, mcp, doc, project, loop or prompt.
--sort <sort>   rank (default), downloads, stars, recent (newly added) or updated.
--limit <n>     At most n results (1-50; the registry's default is 20).
--json          Emit [{ref, owner, slug, kind, name, tagline, stars, downloads, updated_at}].

commands.summary: Print an artifact's root document (SKILL.md, AGENT.md, LOOP.md, ...) without installing it.
commands.desc: An alias of `ahood skill read`, under the name the /ahood plugin commands use: prints the latest version's root document to stdout so an agent can use it once in this session, with nothing installed or written. Works for every kind. Plain mode prints the raw content (control sequences stripped in a terminal).
flags: --json    Emit {version, content} as a single line instead of the raw content.

commands.summary: Show your own artifacts with their downloads and stars, the totals, recent activity and self-evolution counts.
commands.desc: Lists every artifact you have published (public and private) with downloads and stars, sums them, prints your recent activity (GET /api/v1/users/<you>/activity) and how many of your artifacts are evolving and how many proposals wait for review (GET /api/v1/enhancements/summary). The evolution dashboard's yield numbers need a browser session, so they are not shown here: see https://www.ahood.dev/my-evolution. Needs a login.
flags: --json    Emit {owner, totals, artifacts, activity, evolution}.

commands.summary: Add ahood (MCP server and /ahood commands) to Claude Code, Codex or opencode, or remove it again.
commands.desc: With no harness, detects which of Claude Code, Codex and opencode are installed (CLI on PATH or config dir) and asks which to set up. Claude Code: installs the ahood plugin the native way -- `claude plugin marketplace add AlexKay28/ahood-cli#release` then `claude plugin install ahood@ahood` -- or, when the claude CLI has no `plugin` subcommands, prints the /plugin commands to type in a session. Codex: installs the ahood Codex plugin -- [marketplaces.ahood] (ref = "release") and [plugins."ahood@ahood"] as a marked block in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml (default ~/.codex), then `codex plugin marketplace upgrade ahood` and `codex plugin add ahood@ahood` -- and takes out the MCP block, skill and AGENTS.md snippet earlier versions wrote. Both hosts read the plugin from the `release` branch, which moves only when a version is released; an install from main or a tag is moved over. Claude Code updates a third-party plugin in the background only when told to, so setup asks once "Keep ahood up to date automatically?" (default yes; --yes means yes) and sets autoUpdate on the ahood marketplace in ~/.claude/settings.json; Codex and opencode update on their own. opencode: adds mcp.servers.ahood to the global opencode.json(c) and lists the @ahood/opencode-plugin package, which brings the /ahood commands. Not logged in? It offers `ahood login` first. Every MCP entry reads its token from $AHOOD_TOKEN ($AHOOD_API_TOKEN is the deprecated old name) unless you let setup store the token in that harness's own config -- an [mcp_servers.ahood] in the Codex block that replaces the plugin's, the opencode MCP entry, or env.AHOOD_TOKEN in ~/.claude/settings.json -- which it asks about per harness (--store-token says yes up front; --yes alone does not store it). A file setup creates for the token is 0600; an existing one other users can read is tightened only on a separate yes. The token is never printed, and backups have it redacted. Only ahood's own entries are ever added or changed; a file is backed up to <file>.ahood-backup-<timestamp> before it is edited, a re-run with nothing to change writes nothing, and a malformed config or a same-named entry of yours is refused untouched. --remove takes out only ahood's entries and keeps the backups.
flags: --remove <harness>  Remove ahood's entries from that harness instead.
--yes               Apply without asking.
--dry-run           Print what would change; write and run nothing.
--store-token       Store the ahood token in each harness's config (no question asked).
--no-store-token    Never store it; the configs name $AHOOD_TOKEN (a token setup stored is taken out).
--no-auto-update    Do not ask about, or turn on, Claude Code's background plugin updates.

commands.summary: Check each harness's ahood setup, the MCP server, your login and the CLI version.
commands.desc: For Claude Code, Codex and opencode: whether it is installed, whether ahood's config is in place and current, and -- for each one set up -- whether the ahood MCP server answers. Also checks that you are logged in (`ahood whoami`) and whether a newer @ahood/cli is on npm. Exits 1 when a harness that is set up is broken (partial or unreadable config, or the MCP server unreachable); warnings exit 0.
flags: --offline  Skip every network check (MCP probe, token check, npm latest).
--json     Emit the report as JSON.

commands.summary: Publish a new version of a skill, agent, mcp server manifest, doc, project guide, loop, or prompt from a folder containing SKILL.md, AGENT.md, server.json, DOC.md, PROJECT.md, LOOP.md, or PROMPT.md, creating the skill first if it doesn't already exist.
commands.desc: Publish a new version of a skill, agent, mcp server manifest, doc, project guide, loop, or prompt from a folder containing SKILL.md, AGENT.md, server.json, DOC.md, PROJECT.md, LOOP.md, or PROMPT.md. If the artifact doesn't exist yet, this creates it first -- pass --name to set its display name, and --kind agent, --kind mcp, --kind doc, --kind project, --kind loop, or --kind prompt if publishing an AGENT.md, server.json, DOC.md, PROJECT.md, LOOP.md, or PROMPT.md (auto-detected from the folder contents when only one of SKILL.md/AGENT.md/server.json/DOC.md/PROJECT.md/LOOP.md/PROMPT.md is present). A PROMPT.md is checked locally before anything is uploaded: an undeclared {{key}}, or a declared input the body never uses, is refused with an error naming the key. --name is required when creating; optionally also pass --tagline/--tags/--license/--homepage/--repository. Processing happens server-side after upload; this command polls and reports the final published/failed status. The legacy form `ahood skill publish <path> --owner <owner> --slug <skill> --version <x.y.z>` is still accepted. Every flag also accepts the --flag=value form, needed when a value itself starts with --.
flags: --kind <kind>                 skill, agent, mcp, doc, project, loop, or prompt. Auto-detected from the folder's root doc when omitted.
--name <text>                 Required only when creating the artifact on this publish.
--tagline <text>              Short one-line description, used only when creating.
--tags <comma,separated>      Initial tags, used only when creating.
--license <id>                An SPDX license identifier, e.g. MIT, used only when creating.
--homepage <url>              The artifact's homepage URL, used only when creating.
--repository <url>            The artifact's source repository URL, used only when creating.
--changelog <text>            What changed in this version, shown by `ahood skill versions`.
--json                        Suppress human progress lines; print one {version,status,...} JSON object on completion (or {error} on failure).
examples: ahood skill publish alice/pdf-tools@1.0.0 --name "PDF Tools" --tagline "Merge and split PDFs"

commands.summary: Fill a prompt's inputs and print the text, ready to paste into an agent once.
commands.desc: Read a published prompt's PROMPT.md, fill each {{key}} placeholder, and print the filled text -- and nothing else -- to stdout, so `| pbcopy` and `> prompt.txt` both work. Set an input with --<key> <value> or --<key>=<value>; an empty or omitted one uses its default. A required input (one with no default) left unset, or a --<key> the prompt does not declare, is a usage error (exit 2) naming the key. Filling is one pass: a value that itself contains {{x}} is inserted verbatim. Refused, before anything else happens, when the target is not a prompt.
flags: --<key> <value>   Set the input <key> (or --<key>=<value>, needed when the value starts with --).
--copy            Copy the filled text to the clipboard (pbcopy, clip, wl-copy or xclip) instead of printing it;
fails, printing nothing, when no clipboard tool works.
--json            Emit {owner, slug, name, intent, version, inputs, works_with, text} -- the hosted get_prompt
MCP tool's payload -- instead of the text.
examples: ahood prompt get alice/brutalist-landing-page --product "a CLI for agent skills"
ahood prompt get alice/brutalist-landing-page@1.0.0 --product "a CLI" --audience designers --copy
ahood prompt get alice/brutalist-landing-page --product "a CLI" > prompt.txt

commands.desc: Remove a member from a group you own. The group's owner cannot be removed this way -- delete the group instead. Only the group's owner can remove someone other than themselves. Prompts for a typed "yes" unless --yes is passed.
flags: --yes    Skip the interactive confirmation, for scripts/CI.

commands.summary: Leave a group you belong to (prompts for confirmation unless --yes is passed).
commands.desc: Leave a group you belong to. The group's owner cannot leave -- delete the group instead. Prompts for a typed "yes" unless --yes is passed.
flags: --yes    Skip the interactive confirmation, for scripts/CI.

commands.summary: Permanently delete a group you own (prompts for confirmation unless --yes is passed).
commands.desc: Permanently delete a group you own, removing it for every member. Prompts for a typed "yes" unless --yes is passed.
flags: --yes    Skip the interactive confirmation, for scripts/CI.

commands.summary: Capture a new private snap, from an argument or piped stdin.
commands.desc: Capture a new private snap. Pass the content as an argument, or omit it and pipe content on stdin (e.g. `echo "..." | ahood snap create`, or a piped heredoc) -- useful for capturing a whole session's worth of freeform text at once. Prints the new snap's id on success. An unrecognized flag is refused rather than folded into the note; pass content that itself starts with `--` after a bare `--`. The optional structured header (--failed, --worked, --fix, --lesson, --artifact) records what went wrong, what worked, the fix, the general lesson and which artifact it is about, so your artifacts' self-evolution can read them; `ahood snap --lesson ... <content>` (no verb) is the same command. A snap is private to you until you share it.
flags: --tags <comma,separated>   Attach tags to the new snap.
--failed <text>            What went wrong, or what the user corrected.
--worked <text>            What worked.
--fix <text>               The change made or needed.
--lesson <text>            The general takeaway (no names or private details).
--artifact <owner/slug>    The skill, agent or MCP server it is about (optionally @version).
--json                     Emit {id, created_at} instead of just the bare id.
--                         End of options: everything after it is content, verbatim.
examples: ahood snap create "Debugged the flaky CI step, root cause was a race in the cache key." --tags deploy,bugfix
ahood snap create -- "--json broke the parser"
ahood snap --artifact alice/pdf-tools --failed "split pages out of order" --lesson "sort by page index" "pdf split bug"

commands.summary: List your own snaps, most recent first.
commands.desc: List your own snaps: id, a truncated content preview, created_at, a (shared) marker if shared, and any tags in brackets. --tags narrows the list to snaps carrying every tag given (not any of them), matched case-insensitively.
flags: --json               Emit the raw snap objects instead of formatted lines.
--limit <n>          Cap the number of results.
--tags tag1,tag2     Only snaps carrying ALL of these tags. Case-insensitive; at most 8.

commands.summary: Search your own snaps by content.
commands.desc: Search your own snaps by content. Same output shape as `ahood snap list`. The query matches snap CONTENT only and never a tag -- use --tags to filter by tag, which narrows the text results further.
flags: --json               Emit the raw snap objects instead of formatted lines.
--limit <n>          Cap the number of results.
--tags tag1,tag2     Only snaps carrying ALL of these tags. Case-insensitive; at most 8.

commands.summary: Print a single snap's full content.
commands.desc: Print a single snap's full content. Plain mode prints the raw content verbatim to stdout -- no formatting, no labels -- so it's safe to pipe into a file or another tool.
flags: --json    Emit the full snap object instead of the raw content.

commands.summary: Permanently delete a snap (prompts for confirmation unless --yes is passed).
commands.desc: Permanently delete a snap. Irreversible. Prompts for a typed "yes" unless --yes is passed.
flags: --yes    Skip the interactive confirmation, for scripts/CI.

commands.summary: Mint (or return the existing) shareable link for a snap.
commands.desc: Mint or return the existing shareable link for a snap. Idempotent -- safe to run more than once.
flags: --json    Emit {share_url} instead of just the bare URL.

commands.summary: Revoke a snap's share link (the snap itself is untouched; prompts for confirmation unless --yes is passed).
commands.desc: Revoke a snap's share link -- the snap itself is untouched, and re-running `ahood snap share` mints a new link. Prompts for a typed "yes" unless --yes is passed, since anyone using the old link loses access immediately.
flags: --yes    Skip the interactive confirmation, for scripts/CI.

commands.summary: Print a snap's tags, or replace them with the tags given.
commands.desc: With no tag list, prints the snap's current tags and changes nothing. With a tag list, replaces the full set -- this is not a merge, so any existing tags not listed are dropped. Tags may be given as separate arguments, comma-separated, or both; quote a tag that contains a space. Clearing every tag is explicit: pass --clear or an empty string. Each tag prints quoted, so one multi-word tag never looks like two. No confirmation prompt: unlike remove/unshare this only touches metadata, never the snap's content or shareability, and the tags it replaces can be read back first.
flags: --clear   Remove every tag from the snap.
--json    Emit {id, tags} instead of a plain-text summary.
examples: ahood snap tags snap_123 deploy bugfix
